canDo: Can explain a problem, make a request, respond to a refusal, and use double pronouns to avoid repetition in common service situations.
review: Review conditionnel, COD/COI and questions; add the order of double pronouns such as le/la/les + lui/leur.
input: Listening: reception/customer-service conversations; reading: terms of service and short emails.
output: Write a complaint message; a 3-minute hotel role-play.
checkpoint: The exchange goes at least “problem → request → response → alternative → close”.
challenge: Today’s challenge: imagine the hotel room you booked doesn’t match its description; write a polite 5-sentence request (Pourriez-vous… / J’aimerais…) with at least 2 double pronouns (je vous le renvoie, pouvez-vous me la changer); then practise a phone version aloud once and prepare a reply to a refusal.

The only thing allowed is a deduction for use beyond what a trial covers.
Humidity is normal in the other rooms and the residents air them daily, which rules out poor ventilation.
« comme nous l'avons fait pour la chaudière l'an dernier » — while keeping the conciliation committee as an option.
The other side has to answer yes, no or with a counter-offer — « la contre-proposition, c'est déjà une négociation ».
His reason is work, not medical, so « la seconde option ne s'applique pas ».
She looks up a 6 h 40 ticket for 62 euros herself, cheaper than the same-day fare of 94 euros.
« C'est le poste où je ne peux pas bouger » — three days, two people.
